subject: math

objective.text: Find square corners and parallel sides. Use them to name kinds of quadrilaterals.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Use attributes to identify and draw different quadrilaterals including rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms, and trapezoids.

explanations.title: Square corners
explanations.text: The corners of an index card are square corners. Put the card in a corner. If it fits, it is a square corner.

explanations.title: Parallel lines
explanations.text: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart. They never cross or touch, even if they go on and on.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1: drawing parallel lines

explanations.title: Names from attributes
explanations.text: A trapezoid has at least 1 pair of parallel sides. A parallelogram has 2 pairs. A rectangle has 4 square corners.

explanations.title: Square and rhombus
explanations.text: A square is a rectangle with 4 equal sides. A rhombus also has 4 equal sides. It does not need square corners.

examples.title: Drawing a trapezoid
examples.text: Draw a line 8 centimeters long. Draw a second line on the other ruler edge. Join the ends. It has 1 pair of parallel sides.

misconceptions.label: Thinking a rhombus must have square corners
misconceptions.description: Child thinks a shape with 4 equal sides must be a square, or that a rhombus needs square corners.
detection_signals: Says a rhombus has square corners.
Calls every shape with 4 equal sides a square.
misconceptions.response_text: A rhombus has 4 equal sides. Its corners do not have to be square corners.
